purpose: Newly inspected primary neighbors for subsequent courts. This is not a candidate verdict or comprehensive bibliography.

sources.title: The Geometry of Learning Under AI Delegation
sources.status: preprint version 1; venue status not independently established here
sources.inspection: Abstract, introduction, model, stated equilibria and basin result, selected extension details; full proof audit not performed.
sources.known_proposition: A coupled skill/delegation system driven by instantaneous performance can have distinct reliance and skill equilibria with a separating basin boundary; immediate gains can coexist with eventual losses even without incentive conflict.
sources.model_boundary: One learner and task-specific scalar skill, fixed AI quality parameter in the main model, external evaluation and specified skill dynamics.
sources.court_warning: A new name for an endogenous human benchmark, skill/delegation feedback, hysteresis or locally aligned/global adverse dynamics is insufficient. Compare exact mechanisms and new outcomes.

sources.title: Adaptive AI Delegation under Uncertainty: A Bayesian Governance Policy for Sequential Decision Authority
sources.inspection: Abstract, positioning and design/model sections; full implementation and benchmark replication not performed.
sources.known_proposition: Organizational delegation can be a sequential Bayesian governance decision separating model evidence, recommendation and self-reported confidence, and blending AI action with a reference process.
sources.model_boundary: The inspected operational authority representation is a scalar blending weight; do not infer coverage or absence of every endogenous institution from the abstract.
sources.court_warning: Adaptive decision authority and evidence/confidence separation already have direct treatment. Any different endogenous measurement path needs a model-level comparison.

sources.title: Performative Power
sources.status: primary author manuscript; version-specific venue metadata not rechecked here
sources.inspection: Abstract, definitions, learning-versus-steering decomposition, ex-post optimization and multiple-firm equilibrium section; all proofs not audited.
sources.known_proposition: A firm's capacity to change participant outcomes bounds gains from steering rather than learning alone; the framework also considers simultaneous ex-post optimization by multiple firms.
sources.model_boundary: A generic causal power object does not itself supply welfare judgments. Multi-firm steering is expressly present, so coupled controllers alone are no novelty residue.
sources.court_warning: Do not claim provider-benefiting steering or multiple agents shaping the same population as newly identified primitives.

sources.title: Delegation and Verification under AI
sources.status: preprint version 2; publisher proceedings not checked here
sources.inspection: Abstract, contribution statements, main model boundary; robustness sections not fully inspected.
sources.known_proposition: Rational worker delegation and verification can create sharp workflow transitions and divergence between privately optimal behavior and institution-centered quality; stronger AI or verification ability need not monotonically improve institutional quality.
sources.model_boundary: Main model is static and per-task; the paper lists extensions including multi-round interaction. Those extensions require direct inspection before a missing-long-run claim.
sources.court_warning: Rational over-delegation, verification bottlenecks and non-monotone effects are directly anticipated.

sources.title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents
sources.inspection: Abstract, introduction, system/threat model, main state-bound model, non-amplification statement/proof and conditional ascent section; appendices not fully audited.
sources.known_proposition: A grant can constrain changing agents with an immutable protected-effect ceiling and a transition envelope; evidence produced during operation may allocate active authority within the ceiling but cannot raise that ceiling.
sources.model_boundary: Effect containment depends on mediation, sound abstraction, attenuation and monitor integrity. The inspected conditional-ascent section distinguishes reliability evidence from an adversarial upper bound.
sources.court_warning: This is a direct comparator for evidence-conditioned scope, beneficiary-produced evidence, permission partial orders and changing effective reach. Do not assume fresh approval gives causal independence.

sources.title: Agent Incentives: A Causal Perspective
sources.status: primary preprint record; publication version not checked here
sources.inspection: Primary abstract only; theorem assumptions and full text pending.
sources.known_proposition: Causal influence diagrams support sound and complete graphical criteria for several incentive concepts, including instrumental control incentives.
sources.court_warning: Showing an indirect utility path through authority does not create a new instrumental-control theorem. Inspect its graph criteria first.

sources.title: Natural Selection Favors AIs over Humans
sources.status: primary preprint record; version history not yet audited
sources.inspection: Primary record and search-extracted discussion of competition, relinquished oversight and expanding agent access; full text pending.
sources.known_proposition: The paper argues that economic or national competition can favor autonomous AI deployment and expanded delegated control, with selection pressures relevant to system behavior.
sources.court_warning: Selection into broader delegated roles is already discussed. Compare whether intent, deception and self-preservation are necessary premises of the specific passage rather than treating the whole paper as one claim.

sources.title: AI Agent Economics: Can Autonomous Economic Behavior Emerge among AI Agents under Minimal External Conditions?
sources.inspection: Primary abstract only; environments, code and reported outcomes unreplicated.
sources.known_proposition: The reported agent worlds distinguish executable allocation rights and productive work from merely symbolic resources and role prompts when examining emergent exchange and task access.
sources.court_warning: Executable rights affecting future feasible actions already form an empirical multi-agent research object. Model design must distinguish authored incentives from discovered behavioral outcomes.

sources.title: Shadow Learning: Building Robotic Surgical Skill When Approved Means Fail
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Approved robotic-surgery work arrangements restricted trainee participation; exceptional learning practices produced competence for a minority, with implications for expert supply.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract; studies and contribution described there.
sources.limits: Full ethnographic methods and data not audited; first online 2018, issue 2019.

sources.title: Negative Knowledge: Understanding Professional Learning and Expertise
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Expert performance includes experiential knowledge of inappropriate actions and strategies; reflection on errors helps develop this resource.
sources.inspection: Primary article abstract and introduction surfaced through publisher mirror.
sources.limits: Mirror access is not a complete full-text audit.

sources.title: Organizational Memory
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Organizational memory involves acquisition, retention and retrieval, and can be used, misused or abused.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract.
sources.limits: Exact retention structures and detailed decision-rationale discussion require full text.

sources.title: Rankings and Reactivity: How Public Measures Recreate Social Worlds
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Public rankings change institutional behavior through self-fulfilling expectations and commensuration; the measurement regime participates in producing what it measures.
sources.inspection: Author paper hosted by Stanford; abstract inspected.
sources.limits: No claim to have audited all interview evidence.

sources.title: A Theory of Endogenous Institutional Change
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Institution-induced behavior can alter quasi-parameters that determine institutional self-enforcement, producing reinforcement or destabilization.
sources.inspection: Author PDF abstract and opening framing.
sources.limits: Detailed repeated-game mechanisms and historical applications not yet audited.

sources.title: Bayesian Persuasion
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: A sender can choose an information structure that benefits it through a rational receiver’s action without false messages.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record.
sources.limits: Signal-structure commitment assumptions matter; not a universal account of influence.

sources.title: Competition in Persuasion
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Competition need not improve information. A condition on feasible experiments determines when more informative outcomes are guaranteed; sequential and costly information introduce further limits.
sources.inspection: Primary PDF pages1–6: opening counterexample, model, assumptions, Blackwell-connectedness.
sources.limits: Proofs and later extensions not fully audited.

sources.title: Multitask Principal–Agent Analyses: Incentive Contracts, Asset Ownership, and Job Design
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Measured incentives interact with effort across tasks; job design and ownership alter the incentive problem beyond a single measured output.
sources.inspection: Author-hosted PDF opening and author bibliography.
sources.limits: PDF extraction unavailable through one route; complete propositions not verified here.

sources.title: Formal and Real Authority in Organizations
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Information determines effective decision control under formal rights; overload, urgency and other organizational conditions change real authority.
sources.inspection: Harvard primary repository abstract; UCL author PDF opening.
sources.limits: Full model and comparative statics not reproduced.

sources.title: Too Much Data: Prices and Inefficiencies in Data Markets
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Correlated information creates externalities that can induce excessive disclosure; platform competition need not fix the inefficiency.
sources.inspection: Primary working-paper abstract and published-version record.
sources.limits: Working paper2019, published2022; welfare claims conditional on model.

sources.title: Network Stability, Network Externalities and Technology Adoption
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Destabilization of a social network can expand adoption externalities; video-calling adoption and use provide an empirical setting.
sources.inspection: Primary working-paper abstract.
sources.limits: Study identification and results require full-text audit.

sources.title: Adoption with Social Learning and Network Externalities
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Technology adoption can depend on learning from others and benefits generated by their adoption.
sources.inspection: Primary working-paper record and abstract framing.
sources.limits: Specific identification/results not independently checked; do not attribute an AI-deadline result.

sources.title: The Selective Labels Problem: Evaluating Algorithmic Predictions in the Presence of Unobservables
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Decision-dependent observation prevents straightforward human/model comparison; contraction and decision-maker variation enable particular evaluations.
sources.inspection: Author PDF abstract, introduction and available full-text extraction.
sources.limits: No experiment replication; outcome labels differ from unelicited demands.

sources.title: Naked Exclusion
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Rational individual exclusive contracts can jointly prevent entry under scale economies and buyer coordination failure.
sources.inspection: Author HTML abstract, setup, propositions1–2 and explanation.
sources.limits: Equations partly lost in HTML; no new proof claimed; strategic exclusion differs from unintended optimization.

sources.title: Learning and Strategic Pricing
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Competition endogenizes experimentation costs; prices allocate learning benefits over time and support efficient Markov-perfect experimentation in the model.
sources.inspection: Primary Cowles discussion paper abstract; author publication list.
sources.limits: Full proof not read; efficiency is not unconditional.

sources.title: Delegation to Incentivize Information Production
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Delegation to a mildly negatively biased decision agent can induce a proposing sender to produce stronger evidence, improving organizational welfare under the stated conditions.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract, highlights and introduction.
sources.limits: No audit of all mechanism variants.

sources.title: Pilot Early, Commit Late: A Real-Options Model of Enterprise AI Adoption under Rapid Technological Progress
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: A two-period adoption model distinguishes deploy, pilot and wait; capability accumulation and architecture affect the value of staging under a changing frontier.
sources.inspection: Primary arXiv abstract, introduction, related-work sections2.1–2.4.
sources.limits: Preprint; later model and proofs not yet audited.

sources.title: The High-Frequency Trading Arms Race: Frequent Batch Auctions as a Market Design Response
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Continuous serial market design creates a speed race; discrete batched transactions can change the incentive for faster execution.
sources.inspection: Author university publication page, abstract and bibliographic record.
sources.limits: This does not itself establish non-user exclusion under adaptive human deadlines.

sources.title: The Value of Waiting to Invest
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Irreversible investment under stochastic benefits and costs has a waiting option whose value can change the investment threshold.
sources.inspection: Primary working-paper abstract and published-version record.
sources.limits: Working paper1982, publication1986; no replication.

sources.title: What Is Not a Real Option: Considering Boundaries for the Application of Real Options to Business Strategy
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Exploration can change the available choice set and abandonment criteria; a sequence of investments alone does not establish a genuine reversible option.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract.
sources.limits: Detailed cases and counterarguments not read.

sources.title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Thompson Sampling
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Partial-feedback sequential choice creates exploration/exploitation tradeoffs; information-theoretic analysis yields regret bounds.
sources.inspection: Primary JMLR abstract and introduction.
sources.limits: The new disclosure-legibility contrast is not claimed to be a theorem in this paper.

sources.title: Delegating Learning
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Private evolving information creates a tradeoff between learning and timely investment; optimal delegation can require delayed action.
sources.inspection: Primary publisher introduction, model and section4.1; official paper record.
sources.limits: No full proof audit; project investment ends learning in the main model.

sources.title: Performative Prediction
sources.exact_proposition_paraphrase: Deploying a predictor changes the data distribution; performative stability and optimality characterize feedback-aware learning.
sources.inspection: Official proceedings abstract and author PDF opening.
sources.limits: General feedback is inherited; proofs and all assumptions not audited here.
